catalog.thesis: The two registered paths are the movement vocabulary's founding evidence: cross-family movement via admitted bridges (route-dependence, anticipation/prolongation axis) and same-family movement via window traversal (stepwise L/R versus the M successor, linear versus stepped brightness).
catalog.segmentation: Routes are selected gestaltwise (the cadence-as-gesture) and verified hopwise (membership, containment, seam flags). Boundary-layer exhibit routes (d-cycle:*): structural demonstrations of the D-tier M-cycles, verified against the BL-029 probe, not musical routes.
catalog.promotion: Finder-derived routes enter as candidates (derived-path records); registration requires the same human layer as the founders — audition plus recorded verdicts. Machine derivation alone never promotes.
catalog.versioning: Additive-only contract: v1.x bumps may add optional fields or enum members; registered records are never migrated or rewritten. v1.1 (BL-030): added the boundary-demonstration substrate, cycle demonstration move, and exhibit verdict; additive only.

bridge.basis: maintainer listening audition: 5-27 has more character/energy; both legal, selectable as voicing options

verdicts.subject: seam
verdicts.statement: The tonic remains C minor throughout; the leading tone (B natural) pulls onward rather than landing. The crossing reads as intra-tonic motion with the cadence's dominant tension unspent at the seam.

verdicts.subject: interior
verdicts.statement: The three minor chords are perceived as one cadence gesture, not four events; the seam does not fracture the family. The perceptual unit is the gesture while the verification unit stays the hop.

modeAxis.basis: same rotated structure, different focal point; the property only same-family structures have

alternatives.basis: audit-real M successor applications; not in the committed legal-move catalog

triadOverlay.label: C minor triad
triadOverlay.note: the minor third (E-flat) arrives at the Dorian step

paths.schemaNote: first multi-path instance: alternatives may differ in hop topology and legality typing (BL-023 generalizes); no bridge is present because the mode-axis path crosses no collection seam

verdicts.subject: walk
verdicts.recipe: scrum/plan/bl-022-parallel-minor-memo.md §Listening recipe step 2-3: does the mode axis read as re-illumination of one structure rather than a change of object (overlay on and off)?

verdicts.subject: m-demonstration
verdicts.recipe: scrum/plan/bl-022-parallel-minor-memo.md §Listening recipe step 5: does the M jump sound like compressed darkening compared with the stepwise pass?

verdicts.subject: triad-overlay
verdicts.recipe: scrum/plan/bl-022-parallel-minor-memo.md §Listening recipe step 2: does the C minor triad tag carry the third-quality flip as it arrives at the Dorian step?

paths.schemaNote: Boundary-layer exhibit (BL-030): structural demonstration of the D1 (7-22) M-cycle, not a musical route; no listening verdict applies.

alternatives.basis: No alternative exists: the D1 M-cycle is the only traversal structure for these anchors (BL-029); M is row-2-excluded and audit-real. The reverse walk is the same edges in opposite order, still demonstration-typed.

verdicts.subject: boundary-demonstration
verdicts.statement: D1 (7-22) is M-closed: seven anchors in one 7-cycle, tier-, family-, and rooted-Q-preserving; discriminant check PASS over the complete D-D relation set (tier-preserving, family-preserving, D2/D5 twin-separated, D3/D4 Z-partner-separated, rooted-Q preserved). Traversal limitation: the D-tier is fixed-degree-isolated (zero anchor-to-anchor R/L applications), so these anchors are reachable only by M-jump.
